covers.quote: Use initial capitals when writing to ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
The pronouns ‘His’ and ‘Her’ are part of the title. Write these with an initial capital as well.

examples.note: Initial capitals used for title and pronoun.

parts.quote: His Excellency Mr Babar Amin, High Commissioner for Pakistan

rules.quote: Use initial capitals for the titles of high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios
rules.violation_condition: a specific title of a high commissioner, ambassador, or nuncio (or the preceding pronoun 'His' or 'Her') written in lower case when addressing them
when: When writing to or referring directly to high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.
rules.why: G-4: heading states the capitalization rule; covers body sentence restatement and pronoun capitalization rule.

covers.quote: Use ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Her Excellency’ to address high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.

parts.quote: Her Excellency the Hon Dame Annette Faye King, High Commissioner for New Zealand
Her Excellency Ms Francesca Tardioli, Ambassador of Italy
His Excellency Mr Tim Kane, Ambassador to Brazil
His Excellency Archbishop (Most Rev) Adolfo Tito Yllana, Apostolic Nuncio for Holy See

rules.quote: Address high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios with ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Her Excellency’
rules.violation_condition: failing to address a high commissioner, ambassador, or nuncio with 'His Excellency' or 'Her Excellency'
when: When formally addressing or naming high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.
rules.why: G-4: heading states the honorific rule, covering the identical body sentence.

rules.violation_condition: formal correspondence to an ambassador, high commissioner, or nuncio that does not open with 'Your Excellency'
when: In formal correspondence with ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
rules.why: G-1: specific rule for salutations in formal correspondence under section 0dc316eb6c2e.

rules.violation_condition: formal correspondence to an ambassador, high commissioner, or nuncio that does not conclude with 'Yours faithfully'
when: In formal correspondence with ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
rules.why: G-1: specific rule for complimentary close in formal correspondence under section 0dc316eb6c2e.

rules.quote: Open with ‘Dear High Commissioner’ or ‘Dear Ambassador’.
rules.violation_condition: informal correspondence to a high commissioner or ambassador that does not open with 'Dear High Commissioner' or 'Dear Ambassador'
when: In informal correspondence with high commissioners or ambassadors.
rules.why: G-1: specific rule for salutations in informal correspondence under section 0dc316eb6c2e.

rules.violation_condition: informal correspondence to a diplomat that does not conclude with 'Yours sincerely'
when: In informal correspondence with high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.
rules.why: G-1: specific rule for complimentary close in informal correspondence under section 0dc316eb6c2e.

covers.quote: Use the name and official position to address:
diplomatic staff (such as chargés d’affaires and counsellors)
consular appointees (such as consuls general, vice-consuls and honorary consuls).

parts.quote: Ms Susan Grace, Consul General in Chennai

rules.quote: Address other diplomatic staff by name and appointment
rules.violation_condition: addressing other diplomatic staff or consular appointees without both their name and official appointment/position
when: When addressing diplomatic staff (such as chargés d’affaires and counsellors) or consular appointees (such as consuls general, vice-consuls and honorary consuls).
rules.why: G-4: heading states the rule, absorbing the list lead-in and items describing who it applies to.
